post.contentHtml:
About a 30% Discount to Net Assets: What Is the Market Worried About?

Blue Owl Capital (OBDC), a U.S. lender to mid-sized companies, has recently been trading in the high $9 range. The most recent closing price I could confirm is about $9.92, and the one-year price change is about -23.7%. The 52-week high is about $13.57 and the low is in the low $9.80s, so the current price is close to the bottom of its range. I could not confirm today's intraday quote, so please check the actual price in your brokerage app.

What Kind of Company Is It?

OBDC is a BDC (Business Development Company). A BDC is a publicly listed investment company that lends money to mid-sized companies that have difficulty borrowing from banks and earns interest, and it passes most of its income back to shareholders as dividends. As of the end of March 2026, it had invested about $15.3 billion in 230 companies, and it is externally managed by Blue Owl Credit Advisors.

Three Key Numbers

ItemFigure
Recent share price (as of October 20)About $9.92
Net asset value (NAV, end of June 2026)$14.26 per share
Price/NAV ratio (my own calculation)About 0.70x
Quarterly base dividend$0.31 per share ($1.24 annualized, yield of about 12.5%)

Net asset value (NAV) is the per-share value of the company's loan assets after subtracting its debt. In effect you can buy $14.26 of assets for about $10, but it also means the market does not fully trust that book value.

The Signal Sent by the Dividend Cut

Starting in the second quarter of 2026, OBDC lowered its quarterly base dividend from $0.37 to $0.31, a cut of about 16%. The third-quarter base dividend of $0.31 is set to be paid on October 15 to holders of record on September 30. In the second quarter, it also declared a separate special (supplemental) dividend of $0.02.

Second-quarter net investment income per share (NII, meaning interest income minus expenses) was $0.36 on a GAAP basis and $0.34 on an adjusted basis. That is higher than the new base dividend of $0.31, so the current dividend is covered by earnings. Still, the very fact that the dividend was cut once has shaken market confidence, which is a burden.

How Bad Are the Troubled Loans?

  • NAV decline: NAV edged down from $14.41 at the end of March to $14.26 at the end of June. Markdowns on some corporate loans were the main cause, partly offset by share buybacks and earnings above the dividend.
  • Non-accrual loans: These are loans on which interest is not being paid on time, and they stood at 2.8% at cost and 0.8% at fair value at the end of the second quarter. A large gap between cost and fair value means a considerable portion of the losses has already been reflected in valuations.

Judging by the numbers alone, this is not yet a severe distress stage. However, the market appears to be pricing in the possibility of broader credit deterioration across private lending, exposure to certain sectors such as software, and lower interest income from rate changes. This is my interpretation, not an established fact.

Next Checkpoint: November 4 Earnings

The third-quarter earnings release appears to be scheduled for November 4. Here is what to watch this time.

  • Whether NAV held in the low $14s or fell further
  • Whether the share of non-accrual loans increased
  • Whether net investment income continues to exceed the $0.31 base dividend
  • Whether share buybacks continue (buying back shares when the price is below NAV benefits per-share value)

Summary

OBDC offers a high dividend yield and a large discount to NAV, but it also carries doubts about the dividend cut and credit risk. The high yield is partly a result of the falling share price, so whether the dividend is maintained is the key. Major shareholders include institutions such as the California State Teachers' Retirement System (about 3.33%), the New Jersey Division of Investment (3.1%), the Oregon Public Employees Retirement Fund (2.95%), the State Teachers Retirement System of Ohio (2.73%), and Fidelity (2.39%). The National Pension Service of Korea does not hold it. The growth rate of 55.71% in the provided data has an unclear basis of calculation, so it is not interpreted in this article.

This article is not investment advice, and investors are responsible for their own investment decisions.
